title: EXP-0009: what actually helps people climb
parent: Epic: do we recommend the right thing?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the teaching order. Top priority of the catalogue. `trainability`
(`backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs`, rows per band from
`docs/research/improvement-engine.md` section 6.4) multiplies every weakness's priority, and it
comes from research notes, not from players who improved.
- If the result is that the rates which fall first and most among climbers are ones the trainability
rows rank low, we will propose new rows in a comparison experiment of their own (then a major
algorithm version); if climbers' rates fall no differently from matched players who did not climb,
we will keep the rows and say plainly that we have no data-driven teaching order yet.
- Expected cost: staged. Stage 1, on games that already carry Lichess's `[%eval]` comments: no
engine, CPU-hours to stream and profile. Stage 2, sized by stage 1's power analysis; for scale,
1,000 players × 40 games is about 1.2 trillion nodes, about 330 core-hours at 300,000 nodes and an
assumed 1 million nodes a second, a third of that if EXP-0008 allows 100,000; six monthly dumps
streamed once each; no AI tokens; about a week of maintainer time, including a cohort selection
mode.
- Value score: impact 3 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 2 = 4.5 with the staged design (3 at full cost). It
stays first in the run order after the facts epic: no other experiment can change what we teach.
- Cheaper alternative? Partly, and it is used: stage 1 costs no engine time and sizes stage 2, but
its players are those who ask for analysis, so it cannot decide. The research notes behind the
rows are the cheapest answer and are what we use today; this is what checks them.
## Problem
Across real anonymised Lichess players, among those whose rating rose over six months, which
weakness rates fell first and by the most, compared with matched players whose rating did not rise?
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: the Lichess monthly database (many thanks to Lichess and its players): each
game's header rating and the player's own games, under the pseudonym `sha256(salt ‖ lower(name))`
(`backend/crates/lichess-db/src/reference_select.rs`), followed across months by passing the same
`--salt` to `lichess-db build --band-reference`. Today's selection keeps 10 games a player
(`games_per_player`) per band × time class cell, so a climber can leave the cohort; it needs a
selection keyed on the hash alone. No chess.com player's games.
- Runs: now, after EXP-0007 and EXP-0008.
- Primary metric: for each rankable weakness key (`RANKABLE`), the difference between climbers and
matched stayers (band, time class, baseline rate, games played, and the previous months' rating
trend) in the change of the rate per chance from the baseline months to the follow-up months, with
Holm-adjusted 95% intervals over players. Which fell first, against the rating's change point, is
a confirmatory secondary.
- Files and constants: `trainability` and `RANKABLE` in
`backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs`,
`backend/crates/profile-core/src/stats/priority.rs`,
`backend/crates/lichess-db/src/reference_select.rs` and `explorer_build.rs` (`reference_salt`),
`reference_games` (`db/migrations/20261121020000_profile_engine.sql`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The caveats are registered with the design that addresses each: regression to the mean
(players picked for a rise after a dip; matched on the prior trend), rating catch-up of new or
returning accounts (a minimum history), reverse causation (a higher rating brings stronger
opponents who punish more), time-control switching, and rating inflation (stayers in the same
months). What the design cannot separate is stated in the result.
- [ ] The result is reported as candidates to teach, never as causes; the learning experiments
(v0.6) test whether teaching them helps.
- [ ] The longitudinal selection gets its own ADR under ADR-R2-11's privacy rules before any data is
built.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- ADR-R2-9, ADR-R2-11, ADR 0101; `docs/research/improvement-engine.md`; EXP-0004 (#94) for the
leakage controls

title: EXP-0010: rank by points lost per game or by frequency?
parent: Epic: do we recommend the right thing?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the ranking rule `rank-v1` (`RANKING_VERSION`,
`backend/crates/profile-core/src/stats/priority.rs`), which orders weaknesses by `excess = max(0,
mean - median) × (n_unweighted / games) × epl_per_event` against a ranking by how far the rate
sits above the peers' alone.
- If the result is that the frequency ranking predicts the next games' points lost better by at
least the registered minimum effect, we will propose it as a major algorithm version; if points
lost per game is as good or better, `rank-v1` stays and this becomes its published evidence.
- Expected cost: no engine time beyond Tier 2's cohort (at least 200 players with 80 games each):
the same profiles ranked twice through `cli lab rank`, CPU minutes; no AI tokens; about two days
of maintainer time once EXP-0004's design is registered.
- Value score: impact 3 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 1 = 6.
- Cheaper alternative? This is the cheap version: it reuses EXP-0004's registered design and Tier
2's cohort instead of building its own.
## Problem
Which ranking puts first the weakness that costs the player the most points in the games that
follow: points lost per game (today) or frequency above the peers?
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: points lost per key in each player's games after the split date (Tier 2's
held-out games, anonymised Lichess players).
- Runs: now, after EXP-0004.
- Primary metric: the difference between the two rankings in the lift at rank 1 (points lost after
the split by the top-ranked key, over a base-rate ranking), the player as the unit, with a seeded
bootstrap over players.
- Files and constants: `stats/priority.rs` (`RANK_MIN_EXCESS_PER_GAME` 0.02, `MIN_GAMES` 30,
`RANKING_VERSION`), the candidate as a Rust variant run with `ALGO_VARIANT`, never a Python copy.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The frequency ranking exists as a Rust variant on its branch before registration, and does not
change afterwards.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- #94 (EXP-0004), the sub-issue "Tier 2: does the top weakness predict where points are lost?", ADR

title: EXP-0011: are the weekly focus targets realistic?
parent: Epic: do we recommend the right thing?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the target rule of ADR 0091 (`apps/web/src/server/focus/goal.ts`:
`RELATIVE_STEP` 0.25, `MIN_PEER_STEP` 0.1, `DEFAULT_GAMES_N` 20, `MIN_VERDICT_CHANCES` 10).
- If the result is that real players with no focus at all "meet" the target in their next 20 games
more often than the registered upper bound, the goal is met by chance and regression to the mean,
and we will propose a harder or longer target; if they almost never do (below the lower bound), we
will propose an easier one; inside the band, the rule stays.
- Expected cost: reuses Tier 2's cohort and profiles: the rule applied to each player's top weakness
at the split date, then the next N games counted; CPU minutes; no AI tokens; about a day of
maintainer time, plus the way the lab calls the rule.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 1 = 6.
- Cheaper alternative? No cheaper source: nothing published gives the base rate of "a quarter fewer
in 20 games" for a band. Our own cohort is the cheapest one.
## Problem
When Rematch sets a weekly target, how often would a player at that band meet it in 20 games without
practising anything?
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: the observed rates of Tier 2's anonymised Lichess players in the games
after the split date, with the top weakness chosen as the app chooses it (ADR 0091, decision 3).
- Runs: now, after Tier 2's cohort exists.
- Primary metric: the share of players whose top weakness meets its target (the rate at or below the
target, with at least 10 chances) in the next 20 games, with a Wilson 95% interval, against a
registered band.
- Files and constants: `apps/web/src/server/focus/goal.ts`; the series in `weakness_series_point`.
The rule is TypeScript: the registration says how the lab calls it (the rule ported behind the
Rust bridge, or `goal.ts` run through Node), since the lab never re-implements it.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The share is also reported by band and by key, as secondaries.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- ADR 0091, "Show a practice streak" and the weekly focus card (v0.6), the sub-issue "Tier 2: does
the top weakness predict where points are lost?"

title: EXP-0012: do drilled positions resemble the player's next mistakes?
parent: Epic: do we recommend the right thing?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: where the trainer's positions come from: `SOURCES` in
`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (W4.missed, W3.shallow, W3.deep, W7.traps, blunder), all from
the player's own games.
- If the result is that the motifs of a player's drillable positions before a date recur in their
mistakes after it no more often than the band's base rate, we will propose mixing in positions
common to the band (Lichess puzzles by theme); if they recur clearly more often, own-game sourcing
stays and this is the published reason for it.
- Expected cost: reuses Tier 2's cohort, its analysed games and their motif tags: no new engine
time, CPU minutes; no AI tokens; about two days of maintainer time, after EXP-0007.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 1 = 4.
- Cheaper alternative? None cheaper: it uses data the cohort already has.
## Problem
Do the positions Rematch would drill for a player look like the mistakes that player makes next?
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: the motif tags (`move_features.best_line.tags`) of each player's missed
moments after the split date, against the band's motif frequencies; Tier 2's anonymised Lichess
players.
- Runs: now, after EXP-0007 (the tags must be right first) and Tier 2's cohort.
- Primary metric: the lift of motif recurrence: the share of a player's later missed motifs that
match the motifs of their earlier drillable items, over the same share under the band's motif
frequencies, the player as the unit, with a seeded bootstrap.
- Files and constants: `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`SOURCES`, `primarySource`),
`missedByMotif` (`apps/web/src/server/train/store.ts`). The item selection is TypeScript; the
registration says how the lab calls it.

title: EXP-0013: how often is a player with no weakness shown one?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the minimum evidence before a weakness can rank: `min_evidence`
(`backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs`: 1,000 chances for W1, W2 and W11, 1,500 for W10,
15 for W5 and W6, else `n0`) and `MIN_GAMES` (30, `stats/priority.rs`).
- If the result is that clean players (true rate equal to the peers') see a ranked weakness more
often than the registered bound at their first eligible build, we will propose higher minimums; if
they almost never do while Tier 1 finds flawed players late, we will propose lower ones; otherwise
the minimums stay.
- Expected cost: profile only, no engine: EXP-0002's count generator at the peers' rate (ρ = 1),
under an hour on one core at EXP-0002's scale (about 50,000 profile computations); no AI tokens;
about a day of maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 3 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 1 = 6.
- Cheaper alternative? Tier 1's clean controls answer it for nothing, but there are two of them in
EXP-0001's pilot, too few for a rate. This reuses EXP-0002's generator instead of running games.
## Problem
A new player has no weakness beyond their peers'. How often, after 30, 60 or 120 games, does Rematch
tell them they have one?
- Layer: profile.
- Ground truth and data: synthetic event counts drawn at exactly the peers' rate, so any ranked
weakness is a false flag.
- Runs: now.
- Primary metric: the share of clean synthetic players with at least one ranked weakness (priority
above 0 from `cli lab rank`) at 30 games, with a Wilson 95% interval; 60, 120 and 250 games are
confirmatory secondaries.
- Files and constants: `min_evidence` and `n0` in `backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs`;
`MIN_GAMES`, `RANK_MIN_EXCESS_PER_GAME` in `stats/priority.rs`; `min_evidence_met` in
`backend/crates/profile/src/coaching/builder.rs`.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] Reuses EXP-0002's generator and seed scheme with fresh seeds; `inputs.sha256` names what it
reuses.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.

title: EXP-0014: how fast and how falsely do the change detectors fire?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the timeline detectors' settings
(`backend/crates/profile-core/src/timeline/`, `DETECTOR_VERSION` `tl-v1`), which write
`weakness_state_history` and the change states on Progress.
- If the result is a false-alarm rate on flat series above the registered bound, we will propose
stricter settings; if a 30% improvement takes longer to confirm than the registered number of
games, we will propose faster ones; if both hold, `tl-v1` stays and its detection curve is
published; if both fail, no setting of these detectors serves, and the follow-up is another
detector.
- Expected cost: a `cli lab timeline` step (lab-v2) that takes series points, so no engine runs;
then simulated series, under an hour of CPU; no AI tokens; about three days of maintainer time
including the step.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 1 = 6.
- Cheaper alternative? The detectors' unit tests
(`backend/crates/profile-core/tests/timeline_detectors.rs`) check behaviour on hand-made series,
not rates on chess-like ones, and the bench cannot switch a flaw on mid-series. The simulation is
the cheapest design that answers it.
## Problem
When a player's rate of a mistake really falls by 30%, or rises by half, how many games until
Rematch says so, and how often does it say so when nothing changed?
- Layer: profile.
- Ground truth and data: synthetic weakness series with a step change injected at a known game, and
flat series with none.
- Runs: now, once the lab-v2 step exists.
- Primary metric: the false-alarm rate: the share of flat series that reach a confirmed change
within 120 games, with a Wilson 95% interval. The games to confirm an injected change are a
guarded secondary with a registered maximum.
- Files and constants: `timeline/series.rs` (`CONFIRM_P_CHANGE` 0.8, `CONFIRM_REL_CHANGE` 0.15,
`CUSUM_FACTOR` 1.5, `CUSUM_MIN_GAMES` 10, `BOCPD_PRIOR_STRENGTH` 50, `SERIES_WINDOW_GAMES` 50),
`timeline/bocpd.rs` (`DEFAULT_HAZARD` 1/200), `timeline/cusum.rs` (`CUSUM_DEFAULT_H` 4.0),
`timeline/states.rs` (`RESOLVE_STREAK` 10, `IMPROVING_P_IMP` 0.85, `ACTIVE_CONFIDENCE` 0.7).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The `cli lab timeline` step lands with golden files before registration.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers

`backend/crates/profile/src/timeline_job.rs`

title: EXP-0015: is "clearly worse than your peak" a false alarm?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the trajectory rule (ADR 0089): "then" is the `W = min(30, floor(n / 2))`
games centred on the rating peak, compared with the last W by `compareMeans` (2,000 bootstrap
resamples). Its verdict heads Progress, the Overview's `TrajectoryCard` and the coach's
`trajectory` input.
- If the result is that players whose strength did not change are told "worse" more often than the
registered bound, we will propose a rule that does not compare with a selected peak (the start
basis only, or a test corrected for the selection); if not, the rule stays and its false-verdict
rate is published beside it.
- Expected cost: a `cli lab trajectory` step over
`backend/crates/profile/src/coaching/trajectory.rs`; simulated rating series, CPU minutes; no AI
tokens; about two days of maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 3 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 1 = 9.
- Cheaper alternative? No. A peak is a selected maximum, so some bias towards "worse" is expected in
general; its size under this window and this bootstrap is what decides, and only the production
code gives it.
## Problem
For a player whose strength stays the same, how often does Rematch say their rating is clearly worse
than at its peak?
- Layer: profile.
- Ground truth and data: simulated rating series of players with a constant true strength, game by
game with Glicko-2 updates as on Lichess; and series with an injected drift of 100 or 200 points,
for power.
- Runs: now, once the lab-v2 step exists.
- Primary metric: the share of constant-strength series given the "worse" verdict at 60, 120 and 250
rated games, with Wilson 95% intervals, Bonferroni over the three.
- Files and constants: `backend/crates/profile/src/coaching/trajectory.rs`,
`apps/web/src/server/trajectory/model.ts` (kept line for line by
`backend/fixtures/trajectory/cases.json`), `KPI_MIN_GAMES` 10
(`apps/web/src/server/stats/constants.ts`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The accuracy and blunders-per-game verdicts of then against now are confirmatory secondaries.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- ADR 0089, ADR 0083 §6 (the honesty rules for comparisons)

title: EXP-0016: what does the validator miss?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: whether the validator (`backend/crates/ai/src/validator/`) needs new rules
before friends in the beta read the coach, and which.
- If the result is a fault class that gets through more often than the registered bound, we will add
the missing rule before any other AI work; if every class is caught, the validator stays, its
catch rate is published, and stage 2 measures how often the model writes such text at all.
- Expected cost: stage 1 is deterministic: planted faults in fixed texts, CPU minutes, no tokens.
Stage 2, `--live` and never in CI: about 40 adversarial coaching inputs × 3 texts (report, answer,
weekly review), about 120 generations, on the order of a few hundred thousand tokens; each item
records its `cost_micro_usd`; about three days of maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 1 = 4 (stage 1; stage 2 runs only if stage 1 passes).
- Cheaper alternative? Yes, and it comes first: mutation testing of the validator needs no model.
Tokens are spent only on a validator that passed it.
## Problem
When a coach's text is wrong on purpose (a wrong number, an uncited claim, another recommendation
than the computed one, a cause stated as fact), how often does the validator drop it?
- Layer: language.
- Ground truth and data: the planted faults (stage 1) and the computed coaching input behind each
text (stage 2).
- Runs: now.
- Primary metric: the catch rate per fault class on the planted set, with Wilson 95% intervals; the
lowest class decides.
- Files and constants: `backend/crates/ai/src/validator/` (`evidence.rs`, `bounded.rs`, `focus.rs`,
`leaks.rs`, `language.rs`), `backend/crates/ai/src/prompts.rs` (`REPORT_PROMPT_VERSION`,
`prompt_set_hash`), `backend/fixtures/coaching-input/valid-sample.json`.
## Acceptance criteria

rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] Stage 2 refuses to run when `CI` is set or without `--live`; its token count and
`cost_micro_usd` are in `results.json`.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.

milestone); "Check that the recommendation a text names is the computed one" (v0.2)

title: Epic: a pipeline speed scorecard, stages 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
We say the worker is fast and cheap, and nobody can check it. The numbers exist, each in its own place:
per-stage timings in `job_metrics` (ADR 0036, with `stages` from R2), AI cost per call in `ai_usage`,
`lichess-db bench` for the reference pipeline, `cli eta` for one account. A change that halves
throughput or doubles a report's cost would pass CI, and a self-hoster has nothing to compare their
machine with.
## Who it's for
Contributors changing the analysis path or the prompts, and self-hosters sizing a machine and a budget.
## Goals
The cost and latency KPIs of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-factual-deterministic-evaluation-design.md`, section 7, measured in four stages and tracked per algorithm
version:
1. **Engine:** positions a second for one Stockfish thread at the pinned protocol (ADR 0007).
2. **One account:** fixture games imported, analysed and profiled end to end: games an hour per core,
engine CPU-seconds, positions and cache hits per game, and the per-stage p50 and p95.
3. **Reference build:** the `lichess-db` pipeline on the synthetic input, games a second.
4. **Coach:** report wall time, coach first token and total, and micro-USD per report, answer and
weekly review, on a fixed coaching input. Live tokens cost money, so stage 4 is opt-in (`--live`)
and never runs in CI.
Plus the modelled USD per active player per month, with its assumptions in the RunRecord.
## Non-goals
- A latency gate in CI. Shared runners vary by tens of percent; the site shows a trend from one named
reference machine.
## Evidence
- `job_metrics` has `engine_cpu_ms`, `engine_wall_ms`, `positions`, `engine_positions`,
`cache_hits` and `stages`; `ai_usage` has `cost_micro_usd` per call (priced by `PricingTable`).
- The coach's first-token time is not stored anywhere today.
## Proposed design
- Each stage writes into the RunRecord (v0.2), so cost and latency sit next to quality for the same
algorithm id.
- `cli kpi --since <date> [--json]` computes the production KPIs read-only from a live database.
- The Evaluation page on the site (sub-issue) shows the trend.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stages 1 to 4 each have a sub-issue done.
- [ ] Every cost and latency KPI in the spec's section 7 is computed by a named query, tested on a
fixture database.
- [ ] The Evaluation page reads the `bench-history` branch.
## Test plan
- Rust: the stage runners and the KPI queries on tiny inputs and a fixture database.
- Site: the Evaluation page renders from a fixture history.
## ADR
ADR 0104 covers it. A new ADR only for the CPU price model.
## Risks and open questions
- The fixture games for stage 2 must be ours to publish: generated or CC0 Lichess games, never a real
chess.com player's history.
## Pointers
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-factual-deterministic-evaluation-design.md`, section 7; ADRs 0007, 0036, 0093, 0104
- `backend/crates/lichess-db` (`bench`), `backend/crates/cli` (`eta`, `queue-lag`)
- `docs/research/r2-lichess-db-benchmark.md`

title: Benchmark stages 1 and 2: one engine thread and one account end to end
parent: Epic: a pipeline speed scorecard, stages 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
There is no repeatable number for how fast one Stockfish thread analyses positions under our protocol,
or what one account's games cost from import to profile.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cli bench run --suite speed --stages 1,2` in `backend/crates/cli`, writing into the RunRecord.
- [ ] Stage 1: positions a second for one thread at `sf19-n300k-v1`, on a fixed set of FENs checked
into the crate's test data.
- [ ] Stage 2: CC0 or generated fixture games through import, analysis, enrichment and build-profile:
games an hour per core, engine CPU-seconds, positions, engine positions and cache hits per game,
and the p50 and p95 of every `job_metrics` duration and `stages` key.
- [ ] A test runs both stages on tiny inputs and validates the RunRecord against its schema.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/lichess-db` (`bench`) for the timing code; `job_metrics` (ADR 0036).
- Spec section 7 (latency and throughput, cost).

title: Benchmark stages 3 and 4: the reference build and the coach report
parent: Epic: a pipeline speed scorecard, stages 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
`lichess-db bench` prints its numbers in its own format, and nobody measures what a coach report or
answer costs or how long the player waits for the first word.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stage 3: `lichess-db bench --json` writes the RunRecord's shape.
- [ ] Stage 4 (`--live`): one report, five chat answers and one weekly review from a fixed coaching
input, recording wall time, input and output tokens, `cost_micro_usd` from `ai_usage`, and the
dropped statements by reason.

- ADR 0093 (validator false drops), ADR 0062

title: Scorecard page on the site with the trend across releases
parent: Epic: a pipeline speed scorecard, stages 1 to 4

Benchmark results in a file nobody opens do not stop regressions. The public site is where players,

## Pointers

`packages/ui/DESIGN.md`. Spec section 8.

title: cli kpi: cost and latency KPIs from a live database
parent: Epic: a pipeline speed scorecard, stages 1 to 4
body: ## Problem
A self-hoster cannot see what their instance costs per game or per report, or how long a game waits to

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cli kpi --since <date> [--json]`, read-only like `cli queue-lag`, prints the cost and latency
KPIs of spec section 7 from `job_metrics`, `ai_usage`, `report_runs`, `coach_messages` and

title: A low-memory profile: the whole stack in 3 GB
body: ## Problem
The docs ask for 12 GB for Docker, which leaves room for the first Rust build; once built, the
running stack uses about 4 to 5 GB while it analyses. On an 8 GB laptop with a browser open, Docker runs out and the worker is killed mid-game. Most self-hosters analyse one
account and do not need the throughput.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An overlay `docker-compose.small.yml`: one Stockfish thread, worker concurrency 1, smaller
Postgres buffers, no Maia.
- [ ] Measured with `docker stats` while analysing 100 games: peak under 3 GB, numbers in the PR.
- [ ] The analysis results are the same as the default profile's (same protocol, only slower).
- [ ] Documented in the self-hosting docs with the measured numbers.
## Pointers
- `docker-compose.yml` and the existing overlays (`docker-compose.maia.yml`, `*.ports.yml`)
- ADR 0007 (the analysis protocol must not change), ADR 0045 (worker runtime)

title: Epic: patterns and progression
body: ## Problem
A player's profile is a snapshot of twelve weakness families. It cannot say "you started missing knight
forks in October and it has not recovered", because motif miss rates and weakness keys are separate
things, and change detection runs on weakness keys only (`weakness_state_history`, ADR-R2-6).
## Who it's for
Players who want to know whether a habit is new, old or fading, and the coach, which should cite only
confirmed changes.
## Goals
1. **A pattern registry.** A pattern is one versioned (chance, event) rule. Weakness keys and motif miss
rates are registered under it, and a new pattern is admitted only after it passes its ground-truth
suite (v0.3).
2. **Pattern families:** by motif, by piece, by phase and endgame type, by time use, by opening family,
after a loss, and by colour.
3. **A progression monitor:** deterministic change detection per pattern at every profile build.
4. **On Progress:** "Your patterns over time", with the trend, the 80% range, the onset, the recovery,
and the before and after of a focus or of drills.
5. **In the coach:** confirmed changes as citable facts (coaching input v4).
## Non-goals
- Patterns without a ground truth. A family that fails its suite stays unregistered.
## Evidence
- BOCPD and CUSUM already run per weakness key (ADR-R2-6), with onsets and states.
- The motif tags exist per refutation and missed line (`profile-core/src/motifs`).
## Proposed design
The spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-factual-deterministic-evaluation-design.md`), section 10. Each pattern's version is part of the algorithm manifest, so adding
one is a major version with a benchmark delta.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every sub-issue below is done.
- [ ] Every registered pattern has a passing ground-truth suite in the RunRecord.
- [ ] The weekly review cites a confirmed pattern change and never an unconfirmed one (a test).
## Test plan
- Rust: the registry, each family's extractor on fixture games, change detection on synthetic series
with a known change point.
- Web: the Progress view on fixture data, and visual baselines.
## ADR
Yes: the pattern registry and the admission rule.
## Risks and open questions
- Many patterns means many comparisons; a false change somewhere is likely. The admission rule and the
BOCPD threshold must hold the false-alarm rate per player, measured on clean synthetic players.
## Pointers
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-factual-deterministic-evaluation-design.md`, section 10; ADR-R2-6, ADR-R2-7, ADR 0104
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/{timeline,motifs,kpi}`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/progress`

title: A pattern registry: one versioned (chance, event) rule per pattern
body: ## Problem
Weakness keys and motif miss rates are computed by different code with different shapes, so neither the
timeline nor the coach can treat them alike.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `profile_core::patterns`: a `Pattern` with an id, a version, a chance rule and an event rule over
`move_features`, and a registry listing every pattern.
- [ ] W1 to W12 and the motif miss rates registered with their current rules, with replay goldens
unchanged.
- [ ] Each pattern's id and version appear in the algorithm manifest.
- [ ] A pattern without a passing ground-truth suite cannot be registered (a test).
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness`, `motifs`, `types.rs` (`WeaknessKey`, `MotifTag`).

title: Patterns by motif, piece, phase, clock, opening, colour and after a loss
body: ## Problem
"You miss tactics" is less useful than "you miss knight forks in the middlegame with under a minute".
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pattern families: by motif, by piece, by phase and endgame type, by time use, by opening family,
after a loss, and by colour, each a set of registered patterns.
- [ ] Each family has its ground-truth suite in the lab (injected flaws or puzzle themes) and passes it
before it is registered.
- [ ] Minimum evidence per pattern follows the existing rules (`MIN_GAMES`, the ranking floor).
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/bench/src/flaws.rs` (injectors), spec section 5 (Tier 1+).

title: Change detection for every pattern at each profile build
body: ## Problem
BOCPD and CUSUM run per weakness key only (ADR-R2-6). A pattern's onset and recovery are not detected.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `weakness_state_history` generalised to patterns (a `pattern_id` and version), written at every
profile build with `detector_version`.
- [ ] Synthetic series with a known change point: onset found within the stated window at the stated
rate; clean series: the false-alarm rate per player measured and below a threshold set first.
- [ ] Deterministic: the replay suite covers the new rows.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/timeline` (`DETECTOR_VERSION` `tl-v1`), ADR-R2-6.

title: Your patterns over time on Progress
body: ## Problem
Progress shows weakness states; it cannot show a pattern's trend, onset and recovery, or what changed
after a focus or after drills.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Your patterns over time" on Progress: per confirmed pattern, the trend with its 80% range, the
onset and the recovery, and a before and after around a focus or the first drill.
- [ ] Only confirmed changes are called changes; the rest say "No clear change".
- [ ] Rapid first, White and Black split, tokens only, visual baselines at 390 and 1440 px.
- [ ] `pnpm shots`, `pnpm design:check` and a critique by a fresh reviewer.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/progress`, `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`, ADR-WEB-14 (timeline encoding).

title: Coaching input v4: confirmed pattern changes as citable facts
body: ## Problem
The weekly review and the chat cannot say "your back-rank misses stopped after week 3", because the
change is not in the coaching input.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `coaching-input-v4` adds confirmed pattern changes (pattern, onset, before and after rates with
their ranges), with citation tokens.
- [ ] New prompt versions for the report, chat and weekly sets; the old ones stay for stored hashes.
- [ ] The validator rejects a change claim without a confirmed-change citation (a test).
- [ ] A minor or major version bump with a changelog entry, as the policy says.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/coaching-input` (`INPUT_VERSION`), `backend/crates/ai/src/prompts.rs`, ADR 0086.

title: An operator dashboard: cohorts per algorithm version and cost per player
body: ## Problem
The maintainer cannot see whether players on algorithm B do better than on A, or what each active
player costs.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A maintainer-only page: active players, cost per player per month (from `cli kpi`'s queries),
and cohort trends of the guarded patterns per `algorithm_id`.
- [ ] Only for players who opted in, anonymised; nothing per player is shown.
- [ ] Feeds Tier 4 (ADR 0090's held-out positions) for the opted-in cohort.
## Pointers
- The stamped `algorithm_id` columns (v0.2), `ai_usage`, `job_metrics`. Spec section 10.

title: Epic: board, sound and clarity
body: ## Problem
The trainer is silent: `correct`, `wrong` and `pen` exist in `packages/ui/src/audio/sounds.ts`,
and only the game review plays sounds. The board promotes to a queen without asking
(`packages/ui/src/board/board.tsx`: "a promotion picker arrives with the drill UI; queen for now").
The overview carries more than one message, and numbers are styled in more than one way.
## Who it's for
Every player, most of all on a phone and in a daily practice session.
## Goals
1. **Sound:** the trainer plays right, wrong, pen and game end, timed to the piece landing, with mute
and volume in the header and a Settings page.
2. **The board:** a promotion picker, premoves, the drill's right and wrong sequences, piece-set and
board-theme settings within the design system, no overflow at 360 px, a bigger trainer board on
phones.
3. **Information:** the overview leads with the trajectory, one focus and a practise button; the rest is
one click away; one "Not judged yet" list; one number style; "Why this?" on every recommendation.
## Non-goals
- Building before the owner picks. Mockups first, from real screenshots.
- New sounds from samples. They stay procedural (ADR-WEB-17).
## Evidence
- The owner asked for this round after the evaluation work.
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/train-session.tsx` imports no audio.
## Proposed design
The spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-factual-deterministic-evaluation-design.md`), section 11: real-screenshot mockups, the owner picks, then one sub-issue per change.
`packages/ui/DESIGN.md` is the law; tokens only.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every sub-issue below is done, each with `pnpm shots`, `pnpm design:check` and a critique by a
fresh reviewer.
- [ ] Visual baselines updated in the Linux container only.
## Test plan
- Unit: the sound mapping and the settings store.
- e2e: promotion, premove, mute; visual baselines at 360, 390 and 1440 px.
## ADR
Yes: the sound and board settings and where they are stored.
## Risks and open questions
- Sound on page load is blocked by browsers until a gesture; the first sound needs a user action.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/audio`, `packages/ui/src/board`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train`,
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview`
- ADR-WEB-13, ADR-WEB-17, ADR 0092 (the focused overview), `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`

title: Real-screenshot mockups of the UI round for the owner to choose from
body: ## Problem
A UI round built before anyone has seen it gets rebuilt.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Mockups made from real screenshots of the current app (`pnpm shots`), at 390 and 1440 px, for
the overview, the trainer with sound and promotion, and the Settings page.
- [ ] Two or three options per screen, within `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`.
- [ ] The owner's choice is recorded in the epic before any build issue starts.
## Pointers
- `apps/web` (`pnpm shots`), ADR-WEB-10 (visual QA loop).

title: Sound in the trainer: right, wrong, pen and game end, timed to the piece landing
body: ## Problem
The trainer gives no sound for a right or wrong answer, and the review's sounds fire on the click, not
when the piece lands.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `train-session.tsx` uses `useBoardSounds`: `correct` on a right answer, `wrong` on a wrong one,
`pen` when the solution is drawn, `gameEnd` at the end of a line that mates.
- [ ] Each sound starts when the piece's motion ends (the board's motion tokens), in the review too.
- [ ] A tuning session with the owner over three sound sets; the chosen set recorded in ADR-WEB-17.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/audio/{sounds,synth,use-board-sounds}.ts`, `packages/ui/src/motion/tokens.ts`,
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/games/[gameId]/review-view.tsx` (the existing use).

title: Mute and volume in the header, and a Settings page
body: ## Problem
There is no way to turn the sound down, and no page for display preferences.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A mute toggle and a volume control in the app header, kept across visits.
- [ ] `/app/settings` with sound, piece set and board theme (the next sub-issue), stored per user.
- [ ] Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` for any animated control.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/audio/engine.ts`, the app shell (ADR-WEB-16).

title: A promotion picker on the board
body: ## Problem
The board always promotes to a queen (`packages/ui/src/board/board.tsx`), so a drill whose answer is
an under-promotion cannot be solved.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A picker with the four pieces at the promotion square, keyboard and touch accessible.
- [ ] The trainer grades the chosen piece against `accepted_uci` (`drill_items`).
- [ ] An e2e test promotes to a knight in a drill fixture.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/board/board.tsx` (`BoardMove.promotion`), ADR 0090.

title: Piece-set and board-theme settings within the design system
body: ## Problem
The cburnett pieces and the one board theme suit most players, not all; there is no choice.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Two or three piece sets with licences that allow it, credited in `NOTICE`, and board themes made
from design tokens only.
- [ ] Chosen on the Settings page; the board reads the choice; visual baselines for each.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/board/{piece,theme}.ts*`, ADR-WEB-13, `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`.

title: Premoves in the trainer
body: ## Problem
In a drill line the player waits for the reply before moving; in real games on chess.com they premove.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A premove can be set while the reply animates and is played if legal, else cleared.
- [ ] Off by default, on in Settings; a premove never counts as the answer to a different position.
## Pointers
- `packages/ui/src/board/board.tsx`, `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/train-session.tsx`.

title: The overview leads with the trajectory, one focus and a practise button
body: ## Problem
The overview (ADR 0092) still shows several cards with equal weight above the fold.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Above the fold at 390 px: the rating trajectory, the one weekly focus with its target, and a
practise button; everything else behind progressive disclosure.
- [ ] Rapid first and the White and Black split kept.
- [ ] Visual baselines and a fresh critique.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview`, `apps/web/src/server/overview/overview.ts`, ADR 0092.

title: One "Not judged yet" list and one number style
body: ## Problem
Measures without enough evidence appear in several places with different words, and percentages,
rates and counts are not formatted the same way on every page.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One "Not judged yet" list per page, with the shortfall ("Need 9 more games") for each item.
- [ ] One formatter for rates, percentages, counts and ranges (`apps/web/src/server/filters/formats.ts`
or the stats module), used everywhere; a test greps for stray `toFixed` in views.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/profile/glossary.ts`, ADR-WEB-19 (one statistics convention).

title: Why this? on every recommendation
body: ## Problem
v0.2 ships the facts behind each recommendation; the player cannot see them yet.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A "Why this?" disclosure on the top weakness, the weekly focus and its target, each drill and
each plan item, showing the facts, the rule in words and the algorithm id with a link to its
changelog entry.
- [ ] Keyboard and screen-reader accessible; tokens only; visual baselines.
## Pointers
- v0.2's "Why this? data for every recommendation"; spec section 9.

title: No overflow at 360 px and a bigger trainer board on phones
body: ## Problem
The visual baselines are at 390 px; some phones are 360 px wide, and the trainer board leaves space
unused on a phone.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No horizontal scroll on any app page at 360 px (an e2e check like the existing overflow checks).
- [ ] The trainer board fills the width minus the page gutter on phones.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e` (the quality specs), `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/train-view.tsx`.

title: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader
body: ## Problem
The app is laid out for 390 px and has visual baselines there, but nobody has used it as a phone
app for a week. The axe check runs on the report, weaknesses, progress and coach pages
(`apps/web/e2e/game-pages-quality.spec.ts`), but not on the overview, the trainer or a game
review. Animated numbers (`Stat`) already carry their value as visually hidden text. No one has
audited the app with a screen reader yet.
## Who it's for
Players who practise on their phone, and players who use a screen reader.
## Goals
- The axe check covers every main page.
- The trainer and the overview pass a one-week diary on a real phone, with the fixes made.
## Non-goals
- A native app or offline mode.
## Evidence
A daily practice habit happens wherever the player is, and for most players that is a phone.
## Proposed design
- Extend the existing axe check to the overview and the trainer (sub-issue), then the game review.
- A screen-reader pass (NVDA or VoiceOver) over the overview and the trainer, with findings filed.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An axe scan with no serious violations on the overview, trainer, a game review and progress.
- [ ] Touch targets of at least 44 px on the trainer (the existing `touch-targets.spec.ts` check
extended from `/lab/touch-targets` to the real page).
## Test plan
- e2e: axe on the overview, the trainer and a game review; touch targets on `/app/train`.
## ADR
No, unless the axe rules need exceptions.
## Risks and open questions
- The board and the eval graph are SVG; axe may need a documented exception for decorative layers.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e/game-pages-quality.spec.ts` (the `axe: true` routes), `apps/web/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts`
- `packages/ui/DESIGN.md` (the accessibility section)

title: Run the axe check on the overview and the trainer
parent: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader

The e2e quality pass runs axe on the report, weaknesses, progress and coach pages (`axe: true` in

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/app` gets `axe: true` in the route list of `game-pages-quality.spec.ts`.
- [ ] `/app/train` is added to the list with a seeded session (reuse the setup in
`apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts`) and `axe: true`.
- [ ] Both pass with no serious or critical finding. A fix uses tokens only (`pnpm design:check`
passes); anything left is listed in the PR with the reason.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e/game-pages-quality.spec.ts` (the route list and the axe call).
- CLAUDE.md "UI" has the e2e command. About half a day including the e2e stack setup.

title: Check touch targets on the real trainer page, not only the lab
parent: Epic: works on a phone and with a screen reader
body: ## Problem
`apps/web/e2e/touch-targets.spec.ts` measures touch targets on `/lab/touch-targets` and
`/styleguide`. The trainer, where the player taps a board and three confidence buttons many times a
day on a phone, is not measured.
## Acceptance criteria

`apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts`) and checks every button and link is at least 44 px in both

- [ ] If something fails, fix it with tokens (`pnpm design:check` passes) or list it in the PR.
## Pointers

- CLAUDE.md "UI" has the e2e command. About half a day including the e2e stack setup.

title: Epic: a daily practice rhythm
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
The trainer works when you open it, but nothing brings you back. On my own account: 347 positions
made from my games, 8 due on the overview, and practice on one day so far (2 attempts, on
2026-11-23). The only streak in the app is per item (`streak` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`), which the
player never sees. There is no daily goal and no reminder.
## Who it's for
Anyone who knows how the pieces move, up to about 2000, who wants to improve, plays most days, and forgets to practise.
## Goals
- One small daily goal: finish today's session (at most `SESSION_SIZE` positions).
- A streak that forgives one missed day a week, shown where the session is offered.
- An opt-in email in the morning with today's count, off by default.
## Non-goals
- Points, badges, leaderboards or any reward for volume. The research says no points for volume.
- Push notifications or a mobile app.
- Changing the spacing schedule (1, 3, 7, 21, 60 days) or the daily cap.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, "Streaks and daily goal": a small daily goal
with a streak that tolerates a missed day (Lally et al., habit formation), and Duolingo's own data
(not peer-reviewed): separating the daily goal from the streak raised day-14 retention by 3.3%.
## Proposed design
- Data: none new for the streak. It is computed from `drill_attempts.at`, read as calendar
days in the player's time zone (`dayOf` in `model.ts`, the zone from `requestTimeZone()`).
- Rule: a day counts when the player answered at least one position that day. The streak is
the run of counted days ending today or yesterday, where one uncounted day per ISO week is a rest
day. Example: Mon, Tue, (Wed off), Thu, Fri is a 4-day streak; missing Thu as well ends it.
- UX: the practise card on the overview (`_overview/practise-card.tsx`) and the trainer page
show "4-day streak" from 2 days up, and nothing below that. No flame, no confetti: one line in
the card's existing type, per `packages/ui/DESIGN.md`.
- Email: a per-user setting (`practice_email`, off by default) and a send time in the player's
morning. The email says how many positions are due and links to `/app/train`, nothing else.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A pure `streakOf(days, today)` in `model.ts`, with the rest-day rule, covered by unit tests
across a week boundary and a DST change.
- [ ] The practise card and the trainer show the streak from 2 days, in day and night, 390 px and
1440 px, with screenshots in the PR.
- [ ] The daily email is opt-in, has a one-click unsubscribe, and is never sent on a day with
nothing due.
- [ ] A short ADR records the streak rule and the email schedule.
## Test plan
- Unit: `streakOf`, and the email's "who gets one today" query.
- e2e: the card's streak line after attempts on two days (seeded, like `train.spec.ts`).
- Visual: the practise card's baselines at 390 and 1440, day and night.
## ADR
Yes, the next free number: the streak rule and the email (it is the first mail that is not a
sign-in link).
## Risks and open questions
- The email needs a scheduler. The Rust worker has one (`backend/crates/scheduler`), but mail is
sent from the web app today (`apps/web/src/server/mail.ts`). Which side sends it?
- Should a session finished after midnight count for the day before?
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`dayOf`, `SESSION_SIZE`, `DAILY_CAP`, `practiseToday`)
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-card.tsx` and `practise-view.ts`
- ADR 0090 (the trainer), ADR 0092 (the focused overview)

title: Show a practice streak that forgives one rest day a week
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
A player who practised five days running sees nothing for it. The practise card on the overview
says "Practise today: 8 positions due" whether this is their first day or their fortieth.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `streakOf(days: string[], today: string): number` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`.
`days` are the distinct calendar days with an attempt, in the player's zone (`dayOf`). One
uncounted day per ISO week is a rest day; a second one ends the streak.
- [ ] Unit tests: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri is 4; Mon, Thu is 0 on Fri; a streak across a Sunday to Monday
boundary; a DST change in Europe/London; today not practised yet still shows yesterday's
streak.
- [ ] The days come from one query on `drill_attempts` (distinct days, last 60), not one per day.
- [ ] The card in `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-card.tsx` shows "4-day streak"
from 2 days up, and nothing below 2. Tokens only (`pnpm design:check` passes).

title: Epic: answer "Is it working?" sooner
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
"Is it working?" on `/app/train` waits for 30 chances on each side of the first drill and for the
80% intervals to separate (`MIN_CHANCES` and `verdictOf` in `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`).
That is the right bar, but a player sees "Too early to tell: 9 chances in games since your first
drill, and 30 are needed" for weeks, with no idea whether that means three games or thirty. My own
account needs weeks of rapid games to reach it (the hash holds back 20% of positions; on my 347
it came out at 22%).
Invisible progress is where people stop practising.
## Who it's for
Every trainer user in their first month, which is everyone until the first verdict.
## Goals
- Say how far away the verdict is, in games, not chances.
- Show the numbers that are already trustworthy: positions answered, and first-try accuracy on
repeats, with n and an 80% interval like every other rate.
## Non-goals
- Lowering `MIN_CHANCES` or calling a change on overlapping intervals. The honesty rules stay.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 4, "How to measure that it works": a player who
cannot see progress has no reason to keep practising.
## Proposed design
- ETA: chances per game from the player's recent games in the scope (the same counting the
"after" side uses), then `ceil((30 - chances) / rate)`. Shown as "about 14 more rapid games at
your recent pace". With fewer than 5 recent games, no estimate.
- Training stats: positions answered, and first-try accuracy by repetition (1st, 2nd, 3rd
showing), each with n and the 80% interval from the existing rate helpers.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The too-early lines in `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts` carry the ETA in games
when there is a pace to estimate from, and keep today's wording when there is not.
- [ ] A training-stats block on `/app/train` with n and an 80% range on every rate, a dash for no
data, never a fake 0%.
- [ ] Unit tests for the ETA (no games, slow pace, already enough) and for the stats.
## Test plan
- Unit: `apps/web/test/train/copy.test.ts` and `model.test.ts`.
- e2e: extend the "trainer states" test in `apps/web/e2e/train.spec.ts` with the ETA line.
## ADR
An amendment to ADR 0090 for the ETA formula is enough.
## Risks and open questions
- The pace changes: a player who stops playing gets an estimate that never arrives. Show the date
of the last game the pace came from?
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`MIN_CHANCES`, `verdictOf`, the before and after rates)
- `apps/web/src/server/train/store.ts` (where the rates are loaded)

title: Epic: drills for every weekly focus
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
The weekly focus can be any ranked weakness, but the trainer only has positions for five sources:
`W4.missed`, `W3.shallow`, `W3.deep`, `W7.traps` and `blunder` (`SOURCES` in
`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`). Pick "Getting short of time" (W9a) or "Leaving
the opening worse" (W7.prep) as your focus and the practise card quietly serves every source instead
(`practiseToday` falls back when the focus source has no items). The player is told to work on
their clock and handed a mate-in-two.
The trap positions that are drilled are drilled as one move: my own account has 71 `W7.traps`
items, each the single move after the trap, never the line that led into it.
## Who it's for
Players whose top weakness is in the opening or on the clock, which at 800 to 1200 rapid is common.
## Goals
- Every focus either has a drill or says plainly that it has none yet.
- An opening-trap trainer that replays the line from move 1.
- A clock-budget check for the time weaknesses (W9a to W9d), as feedback after each game.
## Non-goals
- Drills for W12 (tilt) or W10 (quiet positions) in this epic.
- A general opening repertoire trainer. Only the lines where the player actually fell for a trap.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, features 4 (opening-trap trainer) and 6
(clock discipline). The clock feature has the weakest drill evidence there, so it is feedback, not
a drill.
## Proposed design
- Honest fallback first: the practise card names the focus and says it has no drills yet.
- Trap lines: a new item kind, a line from move 1 to the trap position as the player's colour.
The opponent's moves come from the player's own game; the player's move passes when it is the
game's move or within 30 centipawns of the engine's best. The final question is the existing
single-move drill.
- Clock budget: per time class, a budget per phase taken from the research (at most 15% of
the clock by move 10, at least 20% left at move 30), checked after each game from the stored
clocks, with the share of games that reach low-time trouble as the goal number.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The fallback is visible (sub-issue).
- [ ] A trap-line session on `/app/train?source=W7.traps` that replays the line, with tests.
- [ ] A clock-budget line in the game review and a weekly rate on the focus card for W9 focuses.
- [ ] An ADR for the trap-line item kind and one for the clock budget.
## Test plan
- Unit: line grading, the budget check per phase.
- e2e: a trap-line session from the seeded fixtures; the W9 focus card.
- Visual: the trainer's line mode and the budget line, 390 and 1440, day and night.
## ADR
Yes, two: the trap-line item kind (it changes `drill_items`) and the clock budget.
## Risks and open questions
- Trap lines from the player's own game can contain the opponent's mistakes. Is that the line to
learn, or should the opponent's replies come from the opening explorer (ADR 0012)?
- Stored clocks are missing for some chess.com games; the budget must say "no clock data".
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`SOURCES`, `practiseToday`), `store.ts`
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-view.ts`
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` (W7, W9)
- ADR 0090 (trainer), ADR 0091 (weekly focus), ADR 0012 (opening explorer)

title: Epic: conversion play-outs against an opponent at your level
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
"Not winning won games" (W5) is the one weakness the trainer cannot touch. My own account lets good
positions slip as Black, and the score in my rating trajectory is slipping too. The trainer can only ask for one move, but conversion is a
skill of many moves: trading down, stopping counterplay, not rushing. There is no way to practise
it in Rematch today.
## Who it's for
Players with W5 among their top weaknesses, and anyone whose trajectory shows the score slipping
while accuracy holds.
## Goals
- Play your own won positions on, against an opponent at your opponent's level, and get graded.
- Show where the advantage collapsed when you fail.
## Non-goals
- Playing full games against an engine. A play-out starts from your position and ends early.
- Running without Maia. Stockfish's `UCI_LimitStrength` floor is 1320 Elo, stronger than many of
our players' opponents, so a weaker Stockfish would grade the wrong skill. Without Maia the
feature is hidden, and the page says why.
## Evidence
[What helps amateurs improve](docs/research/2026-11-23-what-helps-amateurs-improve.md), section 3, feature 3: the player's own +3 positions
that ended in a draw or loss, played on against Maia at the opponent's rating.
## Proposed design
- Positions: the W5 episodes the detector already finds (`w5` in
`backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs`): the first position of a winning
episode the player did not win.
- Opponent: the Maia service (`services/maia`, `POST /v1/predict` with `eloSelf` and
`eloOppo`), playing the most likely move at the opponent's rating from the game.
- Grading: pass when the player wins, reaches a tablebase win (5 pieces or fewer, Syzygy), or
keeps the evaluation in the win band for 20 moves without a drop of 2 pawns or more.
- Schedule: 3, 10 and 30 days, one or two play-outs a session.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Play-out positions are made by the worker from W5 episodes (sub-issue).
- [ ] A play-out session in the trainer against Maia (sub-issue).
- [ ] With Maia off, no play-out appears anywhere, and the trainer says Maia is needed.
- [ ] An ADR for the play-out item, its grading and its schedule.
## Test plan
- Rust: episode-to-position extraction, with fixtures.
- Web: grading as a pure function; an e2e against a fake Maia that plays fixed moves.
## ADR
Yes, the next free number.
## Risks and open questions
- Maia needs a GPU-free host with enough memory; check the self-host profile.
- Engine evaluation every move costs worker time. Evaluate only every few moves?
## Pointers
- `services/maia`, `docker-compose.maia.yml`, ADR-R2-13 (Maia licence and difficulty), ADR 0010
- `backend/crates/profile-core/src/weakness/detectors.rs` (`w5`, episodes)
- ADR-R2-12 (Syzygy), ADR 0090 (trainer)

The W5 detector finds every winning episode a player did not convert, but only counts it. The

- [ ] Stored once per episode (idempotent across re-analysis), in a new table from a migration in

game makes none, a drawn won position makes one, re-analysis makes no duplicate.
