title: Epic: do people actually learn?
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Problem
The trainer schedules reviews at 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days, holds back about 20% of items as a
control, and says "Is it working?" from 30 chances on (`INTERVALS`, `HOLDOUT_PERCENT`,
`MIN_CHANCES`, `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`, ADR 0090). Whether drilling a position makes a
player find that motif in later games is the question Rematch exists to answer, and the beta (the
owner and a few friends) may be too small to answer it.
Every experiment here opens with a value case (the decision it informs, what each result would make
us do, the expected cost, the value score and the cheaper alternative), and it runs only while that
decision is open (the kill rule, `docs/evaluation.md`).
## Who it's for
Players who practise; the maintainer, who has to know whether the beta can show anything before
collecting it.
## Goals
1. EXP-0017, runnable now: how many players, weeks and chances the drill effect and the weekly focus
effect need, so the real-user experiments are designed before the data exist.
2. EXP-0018, with real users: the review schedule and the retire rule from real reviews, including
whether "A guess" answers should count.
## Non-goals
- A simulation of the schedule with a published memory model now. It would mostly return the model's
own assumptions, and the literature already supports expanding intervals, so it is dropped;
EXP-0018 uses real reviews instead.
- An observational study of the weekly focus effect before EXP-0017 says the users exist to power
it; it is sized there and registered only then.
## Evidence
- The held-out items (`fnv1a("holdout:<game>:<ply>") % 100 < 20`) are a within-player control that
already exists (ADR 0090).
- ADR 0090: "A learned half-life can replace the Leitner boxes once reviews exist."
## Proposed design
EXP-0017 is a simulation of the registered decision rules (EXP-0001's method). EXP-0018 waits for
the reviews EXP-0017 says are needed, and its pre-registration is written before that data is looked
at.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every sub-issue below is decided or closed under the kill rule, with its line in
`lab/findings.md`.
- [ ] EXP-0017's numbers are on the trainer's "Is it working?" ETA ("Say how many more games \"Is it
working?\" needs").
## Test plan
- EXP-0017 reruns twice in `.github/workflows/lab.yml`. EXP-0018 reads only opted-in users' reviews,
never a chess.com player's games.
## ADR
ADR 0106; ADR 0090 for the trainer; a shipped change is a major algorithm version with its own ADR.
## Risks and open questions
- Users who keep practising are not like those who stop, so any effect estimated on them is
conditional on staying.
## Pointers
- ADRs 0090, 0091, 0106; `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`; `apps/web/src/server/focus/goal.ts`

title: EXP-0017: how many players and chances the learning experiments need
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: whether the drill effect and the weekly focus effect can be measured with the
beta's players, and the held-out design: `HOLDOUT_PERCENT` 20 and `MIN_CHANCES` 30
(`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`), `MIN_VERDICT_CHANCES` 10
(`apps/web/src/server/focus/goal.ts`).
- If the result is that the beta (the owner and a few friends) can detect the registered minimum
effect within three months, we will register the drill-effect experiment as the trainer stands; if
it cannot, we will change the design before collecting anything (a larger held-out share, pooling
across players in a hierarchical model, or a within-player crossover of sources), or say on the
page that the beta cannot answer it.
- Expected cost: simulation only, no engine and no tokens; CPU minutes to an hour; about two days of
maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 1 = 6.
- Cheaper alternative? A closed-form power for two proportions is quicker but ignores that chances
cluster in players and items; the simulation of the registered rule is the smallest design that
answers it (EXP-0001's method). It also replaces a separate study of the weekly focus effect,
which is sized here and registered only if this says it can decide.
## Problem
How many players, weeks and chances does Rematch need before "Is it working?" can tell a real effect
of drilling from noise?
- Layer: learning.
- Ground truth and data: simulated players with a registered drill effect on the drilled motifs'
miss rate, and none on the held-out ones.
- Runs: now.
- Primary metric: the simulated power of the registered decision rule for the held-out comparison,
by players, weeks and the held-out share.
- Files and constants: `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`HOLDOUT_PERCENT`, `MIN_CHANCES`,
`INTERVALS`), `apps/web/src/server/focus/goal.ts` (`MIN_VERDICT_CHANCES`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] The numbers feed "Say how many more games \"Is it working?\" needs" (this milestone).
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- ADRs 0090 and 0091; `.claude/skills/science/statistical-power/`; EXP-0001

title: EXP-0018: the review schedule and the retire rule, from real reviews
milestone: v0.6 Practice habit and trainer depth
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: `INTERVALS` (1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days), `RETIRE_PASSES` 3 and `CLEAN_GAP_DAYS`
7 (`apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts`), and whether a right "A guess" should count towards
retiring an item (today only a right, sure answer does, ADR 0090).
- If the result is a step whose recall at the due date lies below the registered band, we will
propose a shorter step there or the learned half-life ADR 0090 names; if every step lies above it,
longer steps (fewer reviews for the same recall); if right guesses are recalled later as often as
right sure answers, they will count towards retiring.
- Expected cost: no engine, no tokens; real reviews in the number EXP-0017 sets; about three days of
maintainer time once they exist.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 2 = 2.
- Cheaper alternative? Yes, for now: the spacing literature (Cepeda and colleagues, 2008, on optimal
gaps; Settles and Meeder, 2016, on half-life regression) supports expanding intervals like these.
A simulation with a published memory model would mostly return that model's assumptions, so it is
dropped, and this waits for real reviews.
## Problem
Does a player still find the move when a position comes back on its due date, at each step of the
schedule, and does it matter whether they were sure?
- Layer: learning.
- Ground truth and data: the first attempt of the day on each due item, from opted-in users'
reviews.
- Runs: needs real users, in the number EXP-0017 sets.
- Primary metric: recall at the due date (the share of first attempts that are right) per interval
step, with intervals clustered by player, against a registered band.
- Files and constants: `apps/web/src/server/train/model.ts` (`INTERVALS`, `RETIRE_PASSES`,
`CLEAN_GAP_DAYS`, `Confidence`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, then the
rest of the template; the kill rule applies if the decision above closes first.
- [ ] Confidence calibration (how often "Sure" and "A guess" answers are right) is a confirmatory
secondary.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` whatever it shows, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- ADR 0090; Cepeda et al. (2008), Psychological Science 19(11); Settles and Meeder (2016), ACL

title: EXP-0024: the churn between versions, on the first detector or ranking candidate
parent: Epic: the scientific method for the algorithm
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: the size of the weekly and smoke suites, which EXP-0001 set under an assumed
churn of 0.10 (`backend/crates/bench/src/suite.rs`).
- If the result is a churn whose 95% interval lies wholly below the value at which EXP-0001's rule
first fits a cheaper suite in 9,000 games (about 0.03, computed before the run), we will resize
the full suite to what the rule picks; if it lies wholly above 0.10, we will re-register the
weekly suite's detectable change; otherwise the suites stay.
- Expected cost: the full and smoke suites side by side (`ALGO_VARIANT`, ADR 0111), 10,240 games,
about 70 minutes with 8 engines; no AI tokens; about a day of maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 3 ÷ cost 2 = 3
- Cheaper alternative? EXP-0005 tried the pilot and the smoke suite (28 reference hits) and was
closed unrun: no branch of its rule could move the suites. The full suite's 110 flawed players
give about 80 hits, the least that lets a no-loss result act. It waits for a candidate that
changes a detector or the ranking: EXP-0026's is the first, and both read the same two runs. The
kill rule closes it if no candidate comes.
## Problem
EXP-0001 sized the suites under an assumed churn of 0.10. EXP-0006 measured, descriptively, the churn
of one prior change (`lab/experiments/EXP-0006/results.json`, `exploratory.churn`), a lower bound for
the detector and ranking changes the suites exist to catch.
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: the injected flaws of the full and smoke suites' synthetic players.
- Runs: with the first detector or ranking candidate.
- Primary metric: the share of the reference's top-2 hits at 80 games the candidate loses, Jeffreys 95%.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first, with the
fixes of EXP-0005's review: the budget-bound branch computes its detectable change, and the
run checks the variant was applied to the same facts.
- [ ] The suites move down only on a detector or ranking candidate's churn, or on the largest churn
over the candidates measured.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md` and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- `lab/experiments/EXP-0005/` (closed unrun, its review), `lab/experiments/EXP-0001/`, #100

title: EXP-0025: W1's 80% range at 30 games for players far above their peers (#13)
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: whether the prior cap of `algo-2.0.0` (`PriorRule::CHAMPION`, two of the
player's games) is lowered for keys with many chances a game, which would close #13.
- If the result is a candidate that brings the #13 cell at 30 games inside [0.75, 0.85] with
EXP-0006's guards held, we will ship it as a major version and close #13; if not, the cap stays
and #13 is closed with the measured 0.766 as the known limit, said on the site.
- Expected cost: profile computations only, about 120,000 (EXP-0006's design with the #13 cell),
about 25 minutes on 6 cores; the Tier 1 guards from the smoke suite side by side (1,280 games,
about 10 minutes); no AI tokens; about two days of maintainer time.
- Value score: impact 2 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 1 = 4
- Cheaper alternative? EXP-0006's results already give the champion's side on registered seeds,
and its development grid (`lab/experiments/EXP-0006/dev/`) shows how the cap moves the cells;
the comparison still needs fresh seeds for the candidate.
## Problem
EXP-0006 shipped a prior worth at most two of the player's games, counted at the data's effective
sample size and dispersion: every one of EXP-0002's 20 coverages is now inside [0.75, 0.85], but
the #13 case (W1, peers at 0.0008, true rate 0.023) is covered 0.766 [0.738, 0.791] at 30 games.
- Layer: profile.
- Ground truth and data: EXP-0002's generator, the #13 cell at 1,600 players.
- Runs: now.
- Primary metric: the #13 cell's coverage at 30 games, with EXP-0006's 20 coverages guarded.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first; the
candidate developed on its own seed namespace.
- [ ] EXP-0006's guards (the coverage at the peers' rate, false weaknesses, recall at 2, the smoke
CI rule) registered as guards here.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md`, linked from #13.
## Pointers
- #13, `lab/experiments/EXP-0006/decision.md`, `backend/crates/profile-core/src/stats/variant.rs`

title: EXP-0026: rank missed mates and early traps (#11, #14)
parent: Epic: do we recommend the right thing?
body: ## Value case
- Decision it informs: how W4.missed and W7.traps reach the ranking: the peer benchmark they are
compared with (the opponents' row today, too thin for W4.missed, #11, and with no points lost per
event for W7.traps) and W7's place in `EPL_PRECEDENCE`
(`backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs`), which hands an early blunder that hangs a piece
- If the result is a candidate whose recall at 2 on the `miss_mate` and `opening_blunder` players
is better by the registered ship rule with every guard held, we will ship it as a major algorithm
version and close #11 and #14; if no candidate clears the rule, the ranking stays, and the
scorecard and the site say that both flaws are measured but not ranked, with the reason.
- Expected cost: the candidate changes no fact, so both sides reuse the engine evaluations in
`position_evals` and differ only in the profile builds. A development grid on its own seed
namespace, then one paired run of EXP-0001's full suite (10,240 games, about 70 minutes with 8
engines on a cold cache, minutes on a warm one); no AI tokens; about three days of maintainer
time.
- Value score: impact 3 × uncertainty 2 ÷ cost 2 = 3
- Cheaper alternative? Partly, and it is used: EXP-0024 waits for a detector or ranking candidate
and measures its churn, so it reads the same two runs at no extra cost. A fix without an
experiment is not cheaper: either lever is a behaviour change (ADR 0106). The mechanisms are
already known (`docs/benchmark.md`), so no exploratory study comes first.
## Problem
Ten of the eleven misses in EXP-0001's pilot at 80 games sat in W4.missed and W7.traps. Under
`algo-2.0.0` the 17 misses at 80 games are `miss_mate` 9 of 9, `opening_blunder` 7 of 9 and
`no_convert` 1 of 9 (EXP-0006, exploratory). A player who lets a mate in two go one time in two is
told about their hanging pieces instead, or nothing.
- Layer: recommendation.
- Ground truth and data: the injected flaws of EXP-0001's full suite (`miss_mate`,
`opening_blunder`) and its clean controls.
- Runs: now.
- Primary metric: recall at 2 at 80 games over the `miss_mate` and `opening_blunder` players,
champion against challenger, paired; ship when the 97.5% Newcombe interval of the difference lies
wholly above 0 (EXP-0001's rule).
- Guarded: recall at 2 on the other three flaws, a rank-1 weakness for the clean controls (the
question of EXP-0013), and EXP-0006's 20 coverages.
- Files and constants: `EPL_PRECEDENCE`, `backend/crates/profile-core/src/stats/priority.rs`,
`backend/crates/profile/src/reference_aggregate.rs` (the band reference),
`backend/crates/bench/src/results.rs` ("not ranked: no peer benchmark for this key").
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pre-register before running (`docs/experiments/TEMPLATE.md`), the value case first; the
candidate developed on `--seed-namespace EXP-0026-dev` and frozen on its branch as an
`ALGO_VARIANT` before registration.
- [ ] The guards registered with their margins: a candidate that ranks a clean control's noise does
not ship.
- [ ] EXP-0024 registered on the same pair of runs.
- [ ] A decision in `lab/findings.md`, linked from #11 and #14, and the experiment's `summary.md`.
## Pointers
- `lab/experiments/EXP-0001/decision.md`, `lab/experiments/EXP-0006/decision.md`,
`docs/benchmark.md`, #11, #14, EXP-0024; EXP-0003 changes the priors, a different lever

title: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
Rematch reads chess.com games only. Lichess players, and anyone with over-the-board games in a
PGN file, cannot use it. The Lichess code exists: the importer
(`backend/crates/platforms/src/lichess.rs`), OAuth linking (ADR-WEB-4,
`apps/web/src/server/accounts/lichess-link.ts`) and the `LICHESS_ENABLED` flag
(`apps/web/src/env.ts`, off by default, ADR-FIX-N-1). Lichess accounts were parked by ADR 0040 to finish
chess.com first, and nobody has walked a Lichess account through every page since.
## Who it's for
Lichess players, and club players who record tournament games.
## Goals
- With `LICHESS_ENABLED=1`, a Lichess account works on every page a chess.com account does.
- A PGN file can be imported as its own source, for one user only.
## Non-goals
- Turning Lichess on by default in this epic: that is a maintainer decision after it is proven.
- Importing other people's games from a PGN (a club's whole tournament).
## Evidence
Lichess is free for every player, and OTB games are where club players most want feedback. ADR 0040 says re-enabling Lichess is "a scheduling change, not a rewrite"; this epic
checks that claim.
## Proposed design
- Lichess: an audit page by page with the e2e fakes, fixing what breaks. Ratings are Lichess's
own, so no band mapping; the chess.com peer benchmark (ADR 0080) does not apply and must say so.
- PGN: a `pgn` platform whose games belong to one user, imported by `cli import-pgn` first and an
upload form later.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every app page has an e2e path with a Lichess account against the fakes (sub-issue).
- [ ] PGN import from the CLI, with the privacy rule decided in an ADR (sub-issue).
## Test plan
- e2e with the Lichess fake (`docker-compose.e2e.yml`, tag `@fakes`).
- Rust fixture tests for PGN parsing (clocks, missing headers, variants refused).
## ADR
Yes for PGN (a new platform, and other players' names in OTB headers). An amendment to ADR 0040
when Lichess is proven.
## Risks and open questions
- OTB games have no clocks, so W9 weaknesses are unknown for them and must not count as zero.
## Pointers
- ADR 0040, ADR-FIX-N-1, ADR-WEB-4, ADR 0080
- `backend/crates/platforms/src/lichess.rs`, `apps/web/src/server/accounts/lichess-link.ts`

title: Walk a Lichess account through every page with LICHESS_ENABLED=1
parent: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
The Lichess importer, linking and sign-in exist but have been off since ADR 0040. Nobody knows
which pages still assume chess.com: the peer benchmark is chess.com only (ADR 0080), and copy
like "your chess.com games" is common.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An e2e spec, tagged `@fakes`, that links a Lichess account against the fake and visits the
overview, games, a game review, weaknesses, progress, the trainer and the coach.
- [ ] Every page names the right platform, and the peer benchmark says it is chess.com only
instead of showing a chess.com comparison.
- [ ] A list in the PR of what was broken and how it was fixed.
- [ ] No real Lichess account is linked in any test or fixture.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/e2e/accounts.spec.ts` (the existing Lichess linking specs), `docker-compose.e2e.yml`
- `apps/web/src/env.ts` (`LICHESS_ENABLED`), ADR-FIX-N-1, ADR 0040

title: Import over-the-board games from a PGN file
parent: Epic: more game sources: Lichess accounts and PGN files
body: ## Problem
Club players want feedback on their tournament games most of all, and those games live in PGN
files, not on chess.com.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cli import-pgn --user <id> --file games.pgn --name <your name in the PGN>` imports the games
where the named player played, as a `pgn` source owned by that user only.
- [ ] Variants, games without moves and duplicates (same moves, date and players) are refused or
skipped, and the CLI says how many and why.
- [ ] Games without clocks leave the time weaknesses unknown, never zero.
- [ ] An ADR covers the new platform and the opponent names in PGN headers (privacy, ADR 0018).
- [ ] Rust tests with fixture PGNs.
## Pointers
- `backend/crates/platforms` (the chess.com and Lichess importers to copy), `backend/crates/cli`
- ADR 0018 (children and privacy), ADR 0025 (tiered import)

title: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
Every word in the app is English, written inline in components and `copy.ts` files, and numbers
and dates are formatted for `en-GB` by hand in places (`practise-view.ts` has its own list of
month names). Chess is played everywhere; a Spanish or German player cannot use Rematch.
## Who it's for
Players who do not read English comfortably, and contributors who want to translate.
## Goals
- A message catalogue and a locale per user, starting with the overview and the trainer.
- Numbers and dates from `Intl` with the user's locale everywhere.
## Non-goals
- Translating the AI coach's reports in this epic (the validator checks English text).
- Translating the docs site.
## Evidence
Requests from the beta will decide the first language; the scaffolding is the same for any.
## Proposed design
- Choose a library that works with the App Router's server components (an ADR compares two).
- One catalogue per locale under `apps/web/messages/`, keys by page.
- `Stat` already takes a `locale` (`packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`); pass the user's.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An ADR picking the library.
- [ ] No hand-written month or number formatting left (sub-issue).
- [ ] The overview and the trainer read every string from the catalogue, with English as the only
complete locale and a test that fails on a missing key.
## Test plan
- Unit: the missing-key test.
- e2e and visual: the overview in English unchanged (the baselines must not move).
## ADR
Yes.
## Risks and open questions
- The honesty rules depend on exact wording ("too early to tell", "no clear change"). Translators
need those rules next to the strings.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts`, `_overview/practise-view.ts`
- `packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx`

title: Use Intl for dates in the practise card instead of a month list
parent: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/_overview/practise-view.ts` formats "on 30 November" with its own
`MONTHS` array and `getUTCDate()`. It works, but it is English only and the first thing a
translation would have to undo.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `nextWords` uses `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-GB", { day: "numeric", month: "long", timeZone:
"UTC" })` (plus `year` when it is not this year), and the `MONTHS` array is gone.
- [ ] The output is identical: the existing tests in `apps/web/test/train/practise.test.ts` pass
unchanged.
- [ ] Add one test for a date in another year.
## Pointers
- Only `practise-view.ts` and its test. About an hour.
- Run `pnpm --filter @ci/web test -- practise` and `pnpm format` before the PR.

title: Message catalogue for the overview and the trainer
parent: Epic: Rematch in more than one language
body: ## Problem
The overview and the trainer write their words inline: in components, in
`apps/web/src/app/(app)/app/train/copy.ts` and in `_overview/practise-view.ts`. A translator has
no file to work in, and nothing fails when a string is added without a key.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The epic's ADR has picked the library; this issue follows it.
- [ ] Every user-visible string on `/app` and `/app/train` comes from `apps/web/messages/en.json`,
including the plural forms ("1 position", "8 positions").
- [ ] The user's locale comes from their account setting, then the browser, then `en-GB`.
- [ ] A test fails when a key used in code is missing from `en.json`.
- [ ] The English pages are unchanged: the visual baselines do not move.
## Pointers
- `copy.ts` and `practise-view.ts` hold most of the trainer's and overview's words.
- `packages/ui/src/stats/stat.tsx` already takes a `locale`.
- The parent epic.

title: Validate with 2000+ players
body: ## Problem
Rematch is for anyone who knows how the pieces move, up to about 2000. Above 2000 it hasn't been
tested with real players yet: the thresholds, the peer groups and the coach's tone were tuned on
accounts between about 800 and 1500 chess.com rapid (my own is 824). No point assuming they hold
for a 2200 blitz player. If you're 2000+, run it on your games and tell us where it's wrong.
## The rating assumptions in the code
scale (`backend/crates/profile-core/src/bands.rs:11`). B4 and B5 are as wide as B1–B3 but have
had no real player through them.
- Band offsets: a chess.com rating becomes Lichess-equivalent by a provisional offset, +250 bullet
and blitz, +350 rapid, +300 classical and daily (`backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs:140`,
the table at line 131). The offsets were never fitted above 2000, where the two pools diverge most.
- Peer window: the default comparison is the opponents you've faced within ±150 points of your
latest rating (`PEER_RATING_WINDOW`, `backend/crates/profile/src/peer_benchmark.rs:76`, applied at
lines 236–237). Above 2000 a player meets fewer distinct opponents in that window, so the peer
rate rests on fewer games. The band label of a peer benchmark is `band_of` of the raw platform
rating (line 238), with no offset; worth checking that this is intended.
- Band reference: the Lichess band reference is built per band B0–B5 from a streamed monthly dump
(`band_of` of each player's rating, `backend/crates/lichess-db/src/reference_select.rs:460`), and the
opening explorer buckets games by the mean rating of the two players
(`backend/crates/lichess-db/src/explorer_build.rs:77`).
- Trainability: how much a weakness counts in the ranking depends on the band, one column per band
(`trainability_row`, `backend/crates/profile-core/src/constants.rs:47`). The B4 and B5 columns are
judgement, not measurement.
- Coach tone: one tone prompt per band, `backend/crates/ai/prompts/tone/b0.v2.md` to `b5.v2.md`,
registered in `backend/crates/ai/src/prompts.rs:98`. B4 reads "strong club players and experts",
B5 "master-level players"; neither has been read by a player at that level.
- Maia-2: the service clamps both ratings to 1000–2100 (`ELO_MIN`, `ELO_MAX`,
`services/maia/app/model.py:19`, `clamp_elo` at line 76), because Maia-2's buckets run from
< 1100 to ≥ 2000 (line 17). The worker sends the raw platform rating of each side
(`backend/crates/enrich/src/enrich_game.rs:348`), so every player above about 2000 gets the same
top-bucket estimate, and a 2600 is treated as a 2100.
- The Tier 1 benchmark's synthetic opponents are rated 1400 to 1600 (`docs/benchmark.md`), so no
measured run covers the top bands.
## How the ends are handled today
- Below about 600: there is no band below B0. A 500 chess.com rapid player is 850
Lichess-equivalent and shares B0 with everyone under 900, so the B0 tone and trainability apply;
Maia clamps them to 1000. Nothing refuses or warns.
- Above about 2000: B4 and B5 exist and are used, but no threshold, offset, tone or trainability
value has been checked against a real 2000+ account. Maia stops distinguishing at 2100.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least three players rated 2000 or more (any platform) run Rematch on their own games and file
what is wrong, with the page and the number: the ranking, the peer comparison, the trainer
positions and the coach's tone.
- [ ] Each assumption above is checked against their data and the Tier 2 sample above 2000, and kept,
changed (with an algorithm version bump) or documented as a limit.
- [ ] The README's audience line is updated with what was found, with the date.
## Pointers
- [ADR 0101](docs/decisions/0101-weakness-ranking-floor-and-baselines.md) (what ranks), the README's
"How it works" sections on peers and Maia-2
- The coaching-idea form, for strong players who'd rather describe than code
- Spec section 5 (Tier 2, players from 600 to 2000).

title: Epic: what 1.0 means
body: ## Problem
`docs/SDLC.md` reserves 1.0.0 for the MVP and says it is declared in its own ADR, but nothing
says what the MVP is. Without a list, 1.0 is either never or arbitrary.
## Who it's for
Players deciding whether to rely on Rematch, and contributors deciding what to work on.
## Goals
A written, checkable bar. The proposal:
- a stranger can sign up, link chess.com, and get analysis, a profile, a report and a daily
session without the maintainer's help;
- "Is it working?" has given a verdict to at least one beta player on real data;
- the player can export their data and delete their account;
- a self-hoster can run it from the docs alone on a machine with 8 GB;
- every page passes the accessibility checks of the phone and screen-reader epic.
## Non-goals
- A hosted service or Lichess by default. Those are decisions after 1.0.
## Evidence
The beta's feedback (ADR 0041) is the input; this list is a starting point for it.
## Proposed design
The ADR lists the bar; each line is a sub-issue or links to an epic. The release that meets it
uses `release-as: 1.0.0` and `"prerelease": false` (see `docs/SDLC.md`).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The ADR declaring the MVP bar is merged.
- [ ] Every sub-issue and linked epic is closed.
## Test plan
The full gate on `main` and a fresh self-host from the docs on a clean machine.
## ADR
Yes: the MVP declaration.
## Risks and open questions
- Is a verdict on one beta account enough evidence, or should 1.0 wait for several?
## Pointers
- `docs/SDLC.md` (versioning), ADR 0095, ADR 0041 (private beta)

title: Delete my Rematch account and everything that belongs to it
body: ## Problem
A player cannot delete their Rematch account. `apps/web/src/server/accounts/remove.ts` unlinks
one chess.com or Lichess account, and the "Delete your account?" dialog in
`apps/web/src/app/styleguide/sections/overlays.tsx` is a styleguide demo, not a feature. A privacy
promise without a delete button is not one (ADR 0018).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Delete account" on the account page, behind a confirm dialog that names what goes.
- [ ] Deletes the user and every row that is theirs alone: links, focus, drill items and
attempts, reports, coach chats, sessions. Shared rows stay: `linked_accounts` and its games
can belong to other users too (see the comment on `removeLink`).
- [ ] A Lichess link's stored token is revoked, as `removeLink` does today.
- [ ] A DB test that creates a user with one row in every user-owned table and checks they are all
gone, and that another user linked to the same chess.com account keeps everything.
- [ ] An e2e that deletes an account and cannot sign back in to it.
## Pointers
- `apps/web/src/server/accounts/remove.ts`, `db/migrations/` (the foreign keys and cascades)
- ADR 0018 (children and privacy), ADR 0046 (game read model and access)

title: Export my data as one JSON file
body: ## Problem
A player who leaves, or wants to check what Rematch keeps about them, has no way to take their
data with them.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] "Download my data" on the account page returns one JSON file: the user, links, focus
history, drill items and attempts, reports and coach chats. Games are listed by platform id,
not copied: they are public on chess.com and may be shared with other users.
- [ ] Only the signed-in user's own rows; a test proves another user's rows never appear.
- [ ] The file has a `version` field and the format is described in `docs/`.
## Pointers
- The table list is the same as the account-deletion sub-issue's; do them together or share the
list.
